title: Uisdean Mòr takes the Red Hill
summary: Uisdean, five-and-twenty, takes up the holding of the Red Hill on the western lake shore after those before him, an old line owing nothing to Dùn ìseal or to any king of the hill-folk.

title: Uilleam Faire born on the Red Hill
summary: A boatwright's son is born on the lake shore in the twelfth year of Uisdean's holding, and grows up believing, as every child of that hill does, that the water below it has always belonged to his own people alone.

title: The households dig the ditch across the neck
summary: Every household of the Red Hill turns out to cut the ditch across the low saddle of ground where the hill's rise meets the land, and to raise the oak palisade on the spoil bank behind it.

title: Uisdean tells the watch why the wall stands
summary: Walking the palisade by night with the young Uilleam Faire, Uisdean speaks of the long years of the king and of the valleys brought in to the south and east, and does not say whether the Red Hill will swear when its turn comes.

title: The king's company camps unannounced on the shore
summary: The king comes west along the lake shore with some two hundred spears at the end of a summer, camps below the hill, and sends up no word of his business to Uisdean or to any of the Red Hill's households.

title: The first burning of the palisade
summary: On the last watch before dawn the new palisade catches along its whole length at once in a low, dark, shining flame that no one on the wall can trace to any torch or spark. The hill beats it out by morning with lake water and green hides.

title: Uisdean rebuilds with green oak
summary: Rather than wait out a season for seasoned timber, Uisdean sets the households to rebuilding the palisade at once with green oak cut from his own hill, against every carpenter's word of how badly it will burn.

title: The king's spearmen trade through the winter
summary: Neither striking camp nor pressing nearer the wall, the king's company fishes the shallows and mends its gear through the winter, and trades salted fish and small goods with households of the hill who find it easier than the long carry round the lake.

title: The king's frost
summary: In the early days of an t-Ògmhios, when the year should long since have been past any frost, a single clear night puts a white rime on the whole shore. The hill's old women name it from that morning the king's frost.

title: The second burning of the palisade
summary: On the night of the king's frost the green oak takes in the same low, dark flame as before, and burns in less time than seasoned wood had, leaving nothing standing for the households to save.

title: Uilleam throws the water and never learns whose fire it was
summary: Uilleam Faire is first to the second fire with a hide-skin of water, and throws it into the worst of the blaze without saving a hand's-breadth of the wall. He carries the question of whose fire it was the rest of his life.

title: The king's company departs east
summary: Within the month of Uisdean's swearing the king's company strikes its tents and goes back east the way it came, and does not return to the lake shore.

title: The palisade raised a third time in seasoned oak
summary: With no company camped below to hurry the choosing of timber, the Red Hill rebuilds its wall a third time in properly seasoned oak. It never burns again in Uilleam Faire's lifetime.

title: Dùn ìseal's reciters tell the swearing fuller than the Red Hill's own list
summary: Word of Uisdean's kneeling reaches Dùn ìseal, whose reciters tell it with the fire, the frost and the shingle scene kept whole, fuller than the Red Hill's own spare list ever names it. The Red Hill never quarrels with their telling.

title: Uisdean Mòr dies on the Red Hill
summary: Uisdean dies in his own bed on the hill in his eighty-seventh year, two-and-twenty years after the swearing, having outlived the fire, the frost and the king's two hundred spears.
